recommendations.text: Clinical suspicion of bacterial meningitis mandates emergent evaluation. Classic triad of headache, fever, and neck stiffness is present in <50% of adults. Antibiotics must NEVER be delayed for diagnostic testing.

For Initial Meningitis Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - assess clinical presentation (within 10 minutes) - assess vital signs - assess neurological status (within 10 minutes) - assess contraindications to lp (within 15 minutes)
During Initial Meningitis Assessment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge without evaluation.

Converted from unconditional: antibiotics must not be delayed for LP when LP will take >30 minutes; each hour of antibiotic delay increases mortality by 30% [FORBIDDEN: delay_antibiotics_for_lp] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Converted from unconditional: when CT is indicated (focal deficits, papilledema), antibiotics must be given before CT; do not delay antibiotics for imaging [FORBIDDEN: delay_antibiotics_for_ct] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Empiric antimicrobial therapy should be initiated immediately after blood cultures are obtained. Standard regimen: vancomycin + third-generation cephalosporin (ceftriaxone or cefotaxime). DO NOT delay antibiotics for lumbar puncture or neuroimaging.

For Empiric Antibiotic Administration, the following actions are mandatory: - order lab blood culture (within 15 minutes) - give empiric antibiotics (within 15 minutes) - give vancomycin iv (within 30 minutes) - give ceftriaxone iv (within 30 minutes)
During Empiric Antibiotic Administration, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: withhold antibiotics.
Converted from unconditional: if LP will be delayed >30 min, antibiotics must be given first; each hour of delay increases mortality [FORBIDDEN: delay_antibiotics_for_lp] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Converted from unconditional: when neuroimaging is needed (focal deficits, papilledema), antibiotics must not wait for CT/imaging results [FORBIDDEN: delay_antibiotics_for_ct, delay_antibiotics_for_imaging] (Severity: CRITICAL)
Converted from unconditional: oral antibiotics have insufficient CNS penetration for bacterial meningitis; IV administration is mandatory [FORBIDDEN: give_oral_antibiotics_only] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: IDSA 2024 Section 3; IV antibiotics required for CNS penetration

recommendations.text: If LP will be delayed >30 minutes (CT needed, coagulopathy, etc.), antibiotics MUST be given immediately; each hour of delay increases mortality by 30%. [FORBIDDEN: delay_antibiotics_for_lp, withhold_antibiotics_pending_lp] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Adults >50, immunocompromised, pregnant, or alcoholic patients require ampicillin to cover Listeria monocytogenes, which is resistant to cephalosporins. [REQUIRED: add_ampicillin_for_listeria] (Severity: HIGH)

Immunocompromised patients need ampicillin for Listeria coverage; ceftriaxone alone misses this pathogen entirely. [FORBIDDEN: omit_ampicillin_in_immunocompromised_meningitis, give_ceftriaxone_only_in_immunocompromised] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: IDSA Meningitis 2004; Listeria requires ampicillin; cephalosporins have no Listeria activity

recommendations.text: Penicillin anaphylaxis prohibits ampicillin/penicillin; use trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or meropenem for Listeria coverage instead. [FORBIDDEN: give_ampicillin_iv, give_ampicillin, give_penicillin, give_amoxicillin] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Neonates require ampicillin (for Listeria and Group B Strep) plus aminoglycoside (for Gram-negative coverage); cephalosporin alone is insufficient. [REQUIRED: add_ampicillin_and_aminoglycoside, give_ampicillin_iv, give_gentamicin_iv] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Neonatal meningitis has different pathogens (GBS, E. coli, Listeria); adult empiric regimen misses these organisms. [FORBIDDEN: give_adult_empiric_for_neonatal_meningitis, omit_ampicillin_in_neonatal_meningitis] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: IDSA Meningitis 2004; neonatal meningitis requires ampicillin + gentamicin/cefotaxime for GBS and Listeria coverage

recommendations.text: If HSV encephalitis is suspected (temporal lobe findings, altered consciousness, seizures), IV acyclovir must be started empirically; untreated mortality is 70%. [REQUIRED: give_acyclovir_iv] (Severity: CRITICAL)

HSV encephalitis requires empiric acyclovir; antibiotics alone don't treat viral encephalitis and mortality reaches 70% untreated. [FORBIDDEN: omit_acyclovir_if_hsv_suspected, give_antibiotics_only_without_acyclovir_in_encephalitis] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: IDSA Meningitis 2004; Whitley RJ, NEJM 1986; untreated HSV encephalitis has 70% mortality

recommendations.text: Dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg IV every 6 hours for 4 days should be given BEFORE or simultaneously with the first dose of antibiotics. Reduces mortality in pneumococcal meningitis (NNT=7) and hearing loss.
For Adjunctive Dexamethasone, the following actions are mandatory: - give dexamethasone iv (within 30 minutes)

Converted from unconditional: dexamethasone given after antibiotics provides no benefit in pneumococcal meningitis; must be before or simultaneous with first antibiotic dose [FORBIDDEN: give_dexamethasone_after_antibiotics] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: IDSA 2024 Section 4; de Gans J, NEJM 2002

recommendations.text: Converted from unconditional: oral dexamethasone has unpredictable absorption in acute meningitis; IV route ensures reliable CNS anti-inflammatory effect [FORBIDDEN: give_dexamethasone_oral] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: IDSA 2024 Section 4; IV route required for meningitis dosing

recommendations.text: Dexamethasone must be given BEFORE or simultaneously with the first antibiotic dose to be effective; giving it after antibiotics provides no benefit. [BEFORE: give_dexamethasone_iv, give_empiric_antibiotics] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: IDSA 2024 Section 4.1; de Gans J, NEJM 2002

recommendations.text: In adults with suspected bacterial meningitis, dexamethasone should be given empirically and discontinued if non-pneumococcal pathogen identified. [REQUIRED: give_dexamethasone_iv] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: IDSA 2024 Section 4.1; van de Beek D, Lancet Neurol 2012

recommendations.text: Dexamethasone given after antibiotics loses anti-inflammatory benefit; must precede or coincide with first antibiotic dose. [FORBIDDEN: give_dexamethasone_after_antibiotics_in_meningitis, delay_dexamethasone_for_culture_in_meningitis] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: IDSA Meningitis 2004; de Gans J, NEJM 2002; dexamethasone must be given before or with first antibiotic dose

recommendations.text: LP should be performed as soon as possible. CT before LP is indicated ONLY if: immunocompromised, history of CNS disease, new seizures, papilledema, focal neurological deficit, or altered consciousness.
For Lumbar Puncture and Diagnostics, the following actions are mandatory: - perform lumbar puncture (within 120 minutes) - order csf analysis (within 120 minutes)
During Lumbar Puncture and Diagnostics, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: perform lp in coagulopathy uncorrected.
Converted from unconditional: LP without prior CT in patients with focal neurological deficits risks brainstem herniation [FORBIDDEN: perform_lp_without_ct_when_contraindicated] (Severity: CRITICAL)

LP in patients with raised ICP signs (papilledema, focal deficit, GCS <12) risks brainstem herniation; CT must precede LP. Antibiotics must NOT wait for CT or LP. [FORBIDDEN: perform_lp_without_ct, perform_lumbar_puncture_immediate] (Severity: CRITICAL)

All patients with bacterial meningitis should be monitored in an ICU setting. Repeat LP at 48 hours if no clinical improvement. Complications include cerebral edema, hydrocephalus, seizures, and hearing loss.

For Monitoring and Targeted Therapy, the following actions are mandatory: - admit to icu (within 60 minutes) - monitor neurological status (within 10 minutes) - narrow antibiotics when culture available
During Monitoring and Targeted Therapy, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge prematurely, discontinue antibiotics early, ignore neurological deterioration.
